newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals--Cobalt keeps firming, eyes Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals--Cobalt keeps firming, eyes Zaire.

text.p: Cobalt prices continued the gradual firming trend of recent weeks, Japanese traders said on Tuesday, but they doubted turmoil in Zaire's cobalt-producing region would have more than a psychological impact on prices.

Rebel forces in eastern Zaire have captured about one-fifth of the country and were expected to extend their control into the mineral-rich areas of Shaba Province. Zaire is a major producer of cobalt, with output of about 5,000 tonnes in 1996.

One cobalt trader at a large Japanese trade house said he doubted Zaire's troubles would affect worldwide cobalt availability, noting that a large portion of the country's stocks was moved out of the country at the end of last year.
"I don't think physical availability would be affected even if there were turmoil (in the mining areas), but there could be some psychological influence (on the market)," he said.
"It would be hard to imagine that facilities would be destroyed, although social disruptions could be foreseen," including the pillaging of cobalt stocks, he added.
He said cobalt prices started rising a few weeks ago amid sentiment the market had found a floor after recent declines, although this was not directly related to fighting in Zaire.
"Offers are rising and the market is moving up with them," he said. "Deals at low prices have disappeared."

In Japan, he said demand from the battery sector was expected to rise this year, although in the first two months it had fallen short of the market's very optimistic expectations, due partly to seasonal factors.
He added that, despite wariness over the situation in Zaire, Japanese consumers were not likely to build up stocks ahead of the end of the fiscal year on March 31.
Another trader added that Japanese users were buying in normal quantities.
Antimony prices remained soft, keeping China out of an unattractive market, a trader in Hong Kong said.
"Last week and this week I have heard nothing from the Chinese suppliers because the price is just too low and they have no interest in selling at these levels," she said.
The latest indication available for Chinese antimony, inclusive of cost and freight (c&f) in Hong Kong was $2,100 a tonne, she said.
An official of the China National Nonferrous Metals Import and Export Corp told Reuters last week antimony prices would stay flat throughout 1997, having been pushed down by smuggled product.

Japan's molybdenum oxide market was steady after a recent pullback, with one trader citing rumours that Molycorp of the United States had finally begun to ship material from its restarted Questa mine after several months' delay.
He added that vanadium prices were also said holding steady in recent weeks at higher levels reached earlier in the year.
Trade in Chinese magnesium was termed steady, with Japanese traders working down inventories of lower quality material.
The quality and quantity of Chinese supplies had stabilised, one trader said, as mostly the stronger, more reliable Chinese producers had survived a recent shake-out in the market.
